summary: Changes the review requirements for adding DNSSEC algorithms and records to IANA registries. It extends RFC 6014 to cover hash algorithms for Delegation Signer records and NSEC3 parameters, and also updates RFC 5155 and RFC 8624. The aim is to make the process for these registries consistent.

eli5.summary: This changes the sign-up rules for a club's list of approved DNS security tools, so the same rules apply to each list.

subtitle: DNSSEC digest and NSEC3 hash algorithms now need only an RFC, not a Standards Action, to get IANA identifiers.

tldr.problem: IANA registry rules for DS digest algorithms and NSEC3 parameters still required Standards Action, stricter than for other DNSSEC algorithms after RFC 6014 relaxed those.
tldr.mechanism: The registration procedure for these registries changes from Standards Action to RFC Required, and RFC 8624 is clarified about algorithms defined in non-standards-track RFCs.
tldr.outcome: Algorithms in these registries are now handled consistently, but it is easier to add both good and bad algorithms; RFC 9904 updates this RFC.

today: RFC 9157 is a Proposed Standard that is updated by RFC 9904. It updates RFC 5155, RFC 6014 and RFC 8624.

sections.title: The Registry Inconsistency
sections.content:
RFC 6014 lowered the requirement for assigning DNSSEC cryptographic algorithm identifiers in IANA registries from Standards Action to RFC Required. But the registries for hash algorithms for DS records and for hash algorithms used in NSEC3 records were still at Standards Action.

This document updates those requirements so that DS records and NSEC3 hash algorithms match the rest of the DNSSEC algorithms. It updates RFC 6014, RFC 5155 and RFC 8624.
sections.eli5: Most lists let you in with a written paper, but two lists wanted a much bigger approval. This memo fixes that.

sections.title: Updates to RFC 6014 and RFC 8624
sections.content:
For RFC 6014, any DS hash algorithms, NSEC3 hash algorithms, NSEC3 parameters and NSEC3 flags that are fully described in an RFC may now have identifiers assigned in the IANA registries.

For RFC 8624, the second paragraph of its Section 1.2 is replaced. It now also gives recommendations for algorithms defined in RFCs that are not on the standards track. Algorithms not mentioned in RFC 8624 still MAY be implemented.
sections.eli5: Any tool that has its own written description can now get a number. The older guide is also reworded to cover tools from less official papers.

sections.title: The IANA Registry Changes
sections.content: In the NSEC3 Parameters registry, the procedure for DNSSEC NSEC3 Flags, DNSSEC NSEC3 Hash Algorithms and DNSSEC NSEC3PARAM Flags changes from Standards Action to RFC Required. In the DS Resource Record Type Digest Algorithms registry, the procedure for Digest Algorithms changes the same way. This document is added as a reference in each.
sections.eli5: The sign-up rule for four lists is loosened from needing a big vote to needing a written document.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The change makes it easier to add both good and bad algorithms, and the RFC says it is impossible to weigh the net security impact. It warns that administrators of signed zones and validating resolvers should not base security decisions on IANA registry contents, since more algorithms there may not have had IETF review. Safety should be judged from the security literature.
sections.eli5: Being on the list does not mean something is safe, so read about it before trusting it.
